For anybody that works in the tech industry like myself whether you're a Network Admin, Software Developer or someone that is comfortable using a Linux Terminal this will be a walk in the park for real.

If you don't know how to use command line then you will struggle with this game.

I am impressed that the game is able to capture the various amount of technicals like ip addresses, bash commands, file systems etc.

However, some improvements would be great like:
- implementing even more bash commands like "touch", "mkdir", "chown"
- creating your own dns lookup so you can connect to other nodes more easily
- chaining bash commands together like "SSHCrack 22 & FTPBounce 21"
- writing your own program, script or macro to automate things like auto-deleting log files

Overall I enjoyed this game, but that is only because I work with command lines, pwsh and bash all the time.

This game more than any other I've ever played makes me feel like a hacker from the movies, but it does a good job of keeping it somewhat grounded in actual computer science. You can do most of the game through a UI, but if you prefer to do everything in the terminal, you can. The hacking tools are mostly just cool animations (and they are VERY cool), but the game isn't as simple as just typing the command for whatever tool you need and waiting. The game won't always give you easy breadcrumbs to follow, and you may have to search through log files for an IP address to move on. Having a little bit of computer science knowledge is not necessary, but definitely helps. Hacknet does a perfect job of simulating "hacking" in a way that doesn't feel too easy or too hard, and above all, it looks great.

It's.. well, it's certainly worth only $10, maybe $5. It's not very long and the game relies more on pretty looking interfaces and bits of flavor in much of the random, non-plot related text you'll read. The soundtrack slaps, I'll give it that, and I enjoyed pretty much every track along with the music shifting as you progress through the game (with a surprise cameo song from one of my all-time favorite bands near the end). 

It's cool that you can use basic UNIX syntax to navigate most of the game, but it is just that: incredibly basic. The 'hacking' is just running specific tools on specific ports using the exact same commands each time, with a limited amount of RAM at any given time so you can only run two or three tools at once. Also you have in-game notes where every single line somehow takes up like 30 megabytes of space, on a maximum of 761 MB of RAM that can never be upgraded. I guess it was encouragement to stay concise and keep your memory area clean, but it still felt weird. 

You do a little delving into the contents of files to find clues and such which is cool, but for the most part there wasn't a whole lot of thought that goes into progressing in this game as you kind of just did one of a few things that you've already done each of before, probably not even 15 minutes ago. 

Still, if you're interested in the genre, it's a pretty good place to start.

Great Game, Enjoyed every minute of it. Its a good way to kill several hours!! wish there was more content and missions...

1. You can't finish all contracts. At some point the game will just tell you "You're good enough for more difficult tasks" and a main quest will trigger, blocking you from accepting new quests. You can never go back and you can't do them after the final mission.

2. You can't create files or directories. Organizing your downloaded files is annoying because you can only use the pre-defined ones. In one contract you're supposed to forge a file, and that works by downloading a file and editing the copy...

3. You can't remove directories. There's almost never a need to do so, but when you need to remove the contents from a directory with multiple subdirectories, you need to access each subdir individually and remove the contents.

4. Autocomplete doesn't add a whitespace after the autocompleteted word. Confusing as hell for a regular terminal user.

5. The final mission consists of multiple phases, which each one explaining your next goal. In phase 3 you're supposed to send a password but you aren't told so. I just used the password I found to login and continued my quest. After a while I got stuck, and after more than an hour I finally looked into a walkthrough - and learnt that I needed to send the password instead of entering it, and that had already solved the final mission by myself over an hour ago. At least I could just click the "complete quest" button 4 times in a row to trigger the ending.

6. The gameplay is quite repetetive. Connect to a server, open the closed ports (which always works the same, for all of them), find the file you need. There are only 2 missions that go beyond that and actually force you to think: The final mission, and the mission before. That doesn't really speak for the game.

7. The map is just plain awful. It's cluttered with nodes from earlier contracts which you never need to connect to anymore. Literally hardest part of the game is finding the correct node on the map.

8. Secrets. Don't get me wrong, secrets are great. But I looked into a guide after finishing the game, and some secrets didn't trigger for me although I definitely satisfied their conditions. So maybe I shouldn't have written "Secrets", but "Bugs". Furthermore, some secrets get you hyped, and when you finally solve their puzzle, you get... a digital clock that even uses up your RAM?

9. Alt+Tab closes the game.

I completed the game in a single session. It was kinda fun, although way too easy. But damn, some of the issues I just mentioned are pissing me off and I'm not going to play the DLC or any user-created mod.
